final_answer:
Two high-risk user requirements are not currently verified: **URS-EBR-009** and **URS-INC-004**.

**URS-EBR-009** (target MOI outside 4.0–6.0 TU/cell must be rejected for GMP runs) has no verifying test. The only link to it is a `TRACE` to CS-EBR-03, and no test case verifies CS-EBR-03. The nearest test, TC-OQ-EBR-04 (vector volume calculation, TX-0083 PASS), verifies URS-EBR-007 and CS-EBR-02. Its 2.5–10 TU/cell range does not test rejection at the 4.0–6.0 boundary. It is linked to high risks FM-05 (MOI above target) and FRA-042 (function fails), so this is a gap.

**URS-INC-004** (door-open alarm within 60 s) is linked to TC-OQ-INC-04, which failed on INC-03. TX-0023 recorded the alarm at 142 s against the 60 s limit. The other three chambers passed (TX-0021, TX-0022, TX-0024). DEV-26-011 was closed as a minor deviation with a root cause of a misaligned door switch, and it states that the INC-03 door alarm function was not verified. No passing re-execution exists. The protocol is "approved with exception," not verified. DEV-26-033 (a later major deviation) also found the INC-03 door not fully latched, which reinforces the concern. It is linked to high risks FM-16 and FRA-004.

The other 24 URS items linked to HIGH-class risks have at least one PASS execution on an approved test case, either directly or through a CS/FS specification that traces to them. Among these, URS-INC-001 and URS-INC-003 were verified on INC-01, INC-02 and INC-04, because the INC-03 failure only affected the door-open alarm.

Two high-risk user requirements are not currently verified: **URS-EBR-009** and **URS-INC-004**.

**URS-EBR-009** (target MOI outside 4.0–6.0 TU/cell must be rejected for GMP runs) has no verifying test. The only link to it is a `TRACE` to CS-EBR-03, and no test case verifies CS-EBR-03. The nearest test, TC-OQ-EBR-04 (vector volume calculation, TX-0083 PASS), verifies URS-EBR-007 and CS-EBR-02. Its 2.5–10 TU/cell range does not test rejection at the 4.0–6.0 boundary. It is linked to high risks FM-05 (MOI above target) and FRA-042 (function fails), so this is a gap.

**URS-INC-004** (door-open alarm within 60 s) is linked to TC-OQ-INC-04, which failed on INC-03. TX-0023 recorded the alarm at 142 s against the 60 s limit. The other three chambers passed (TX-0021, TX-0022, TX-0024). DEV-26-011 was closed as a minor deviation with a root cause of a misaligned door switch, and it states that the INC-03 door alarm function was not verified. No passing re-execution exists. The protocol is "approved with exception," not verified. DEV-26-033 (a later major deviation) also found the INC-03 door not fully latched, which reinforces the concern. It is linked to high risks FM-16 and FRA-004.

The other 24 URS items linked to HIGH-class risks have at least one PASS execution on an approved test case, either directly or through a CS/FS specification that traces to them. Among these, URS-INC-001 and URS-INC-003 were verified on INC-01, INC-02 and INC-04, because the INC-03 failure only affected the door-open alarm.
